Scientific review and evidence repair

Source: vignettes/scientific-review.Rmd
scientific-review.Rmd

Tempest can review a bounded selection of claims before publishing either a STORM report or a Co-STORM session. Citation verification asks whether a source supports a statement. Scientific review asks whether the statement has an unstated assumption, a methodological flaw, or a conflict that needs more evidence. The two judgments remain separate.

Enable review 

library(tempest)

config <- tempest_config(
  research_review = TRUE,
  repair_evidence = TRUE,
  max_review_claims = 5,
  review_concurrency = 2
)

research <- tempest_run(
  "What evidence supports the reproducibility of this measurement method?",
  config = config
)
cat(tempest_report(research))
reviews <- tempest_claim_reviews(research)

The same configuration works with tempest_session(). Review runs when the session is published, after the conversation has supplied its research claims. The bundled app exposes the controls in its settings.

session <- tempest_session("Measurement reproducibility", config = config)
session$step("Compare the assumptions and validation evidence.")
session$publish()
tempest_claim_reviews(session)

Review is off by default. The limit is 1–20 claims, with 1–4 independent claim reviews in flight. Each selected claim receives an initial review and a separate adjudication. Enabling repair permits at most one search and two fetched sources per selected claim. This bounds requests and retrieval work, rather than making a promise about token cost or elapsed time. Cancellation is checked between operations; it cannot interrupt a synchronous retrieval call already running. An already-started model request can finish, but its late result cannot start follow-up work or publish a review after cancellation. A dossier contains at most 12 sources and 20,000 characters per source. It is bounded context, not a claim that every method or result in a paper was read. Custom retrievers used for repair must return captured resources without mutating the publication workspace; Tempest admits validated additions itself. Accepted Graft knowledge remains outside review dossiers. A knowledge-backed run can review claims grounded in retrieved sources, but accepted records are not added as optional evidence. A selected claim that requires an accepted record as evidence fails explicitly before review calls begin.

Read the result

The report’s Scientific review section distinguishes:

  • Concern confirmed by adjudicator: the adjudicator found evidence for the reviewer’s specific concern. It is still a model judgment for human review.
  • Concern dismissed by adjudicator: additional context did not support the proposed flaw.
  • Unresolved: the available evidence could not settle the question.
  • No issue found: no issue was identified within this review’s scope and budget. This does not certify correctness.

Only selected claims are reviewed, with contradicted and weakly supported claims selected first after citation verification. A completed evidence search means retrieval finished, not that the research question was resolved. A failed retrieval stops publication; empty and budget-limited searches retain distinct outcomes. Source excerpts and exact quotes accompany findings; unsupported source identifiers and invented quotes fail validation.

tempest_claim_reviews() returns versioned plain records with the claim, captured source excerpts and hashes, reviewer and adjudicator outputs, search outcome, model identifiers, and dsprrr program identities. Their content hashes bind the report to the retained records. Saving and resuming a session retains these records without rerunning published research. Research artifacts carry the advisory records alongside their proof; they are not materialized as accepted claims or claim-support judgments.

Evaluate changes before adopting them

The repository includes tools/research-eval.R and a synthetic corpus under inst/extdata/research-eval/. These cases test support, scope, caveats, contradictions, abstention, and misleading evidence. They are engineering fixtures, not human-adjudicated scientific gold data.

The developer harness separates topic-disjoint training, validation, and test sets and supports opt-in dsprrr optimization. Keep held-out examples out of prompt optimization, inspect generated prompts, and measure false support separately from coverage. Package tests run without API keys or network calls. Passing them verifies implementation behavior; it does not establish an improvement in a model’s scientific accuracy.

The review design draws on Google’s Deep Review and the retrieval-feedback approach in OpenScholar. These are design inspirations, not evidence that Tempest reproduces their published results.
